label: Microsoft Outlook Calendar
description: Arcade.dev LLM tools for Outlook Calendar

tools.name: CancelEvent
tools.description:
Cancel a meeting you organize and email a cancellation to every invitee.

Irreversible. Invitees keep a cancelled copy. Refused when nobody else is
invited. this_and_future ends the series the day before the given date, so
invitees get an updated invitation instead, with no note.

Use is_organizer, attendees, event_type and series_master_id from an earlier
read to choose this tool and scope. Only events in your own mailbox, not
shared or delegated calendars.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: The meeting's event_id, exactly as an earlier read returned it.

parameters.name: note
parameters.description: Text included verbatim in the cancellation. Blank sends none.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: For a repeating meeting: instance (this date), series (every date) or this_and_future (this date and later). Required when it repeats; omit otherwise.

output.description: The meeting as read before cancelling, invitees notified, whether a note was sent, and the scope applied.

note.value: Due to a scheduling conflict, I need to cancel this meeting. Apologies for any inconvenience. We will reschedule soon.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: CreateEvent
tools.description:
Create an event in the authenticated user's default calendar.

Book only at a time the user gave or picked, never one you chose. If no time was given,
propose times and let the user pick first.

body is stored as plain text unless body_format says html, in which case it is
stored as markup and rendered rather than shown literally.

Copying a description from an event that was read means passing that event's
body_html as body with body_format html. Its body field is the same description
with the markup stripped, so an agenda copied from there arrives with its links,
lists and emphasis gone.

Ignores timezone offsets provided in the start_date_time and end_date_time parameters.
Instead, uses the user's default calendar timezone to filter events.
If the user has not set a timezone for their calendar, then the timezone will be UTC.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: The text of the event's subject (title) line.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: The description of the event. To reuse the description of an event that was read, pass that event's body_html here and set body_format to html: its body field is the same description with every link, list and emphasis stripped out, so passing that instead silently loses the formatting. Otherwise pass the text to store, which is kept as written.

parameters.name: start_date_time
parameters.description: The datetime of the event's start, represented in ISO 8601 format. Timezone offset is ignored. For example, 2025-04-25T13:00:00

parameters.name: end_date_time
parameters.description: The datetime of the event's end, represented in ISO 8601 format. Timezone offset is ignored. For example, 2025-04-25T13:30:00

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: The location of the event

parameters.name: attendee_emails
parameters.description: The email addresses of the attendees of the event. Must be valid email addresses e.g., username@domain.com.

parameters.name: is_online_meeting
parameters.description: Whether Outlook should host an online meeting for this event and generate its join link. Ignored when custom_meeting_url is given. Defaults to False

parameters.name: custom_meeting_url
parameters.description: A join link to use instead of one Outlook generates. It is appended to body rather than stored as an Outlook meeting, so the created event comes back with is_online_meeting False and an empty online_meeting_join_url -- the link is in the description: in body when body_format is plain_text, and in body_html when it is html. Leave unset and set is_online_meeting to True to have Outlook generate one

parameters.name: body_format
parameters.description: The form the body argument is written in. Set html only when the body you are passing actually carries HTML tags, as the body_html of an event that was read does -- declaring html over plain words stores them marked as markup and they render wrong. plain_text stores the body as written, escaping anything that looks like markup. Defaults to plain_text.

output.description: The created event, carrying the same fields a single-event read returns.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: FindMeetingTimes
tools.description:
Propose times when a group could meet. Books nothing. Use it to find a time, and to set up
or schedule a meeting when no time is given: offer the slots and let the user pick one.

Returns up to max_candidates slots, best first. Each slot counts how many attendees are free
and names those whose availability is unknown, so it answers per-slot who can make it.

Times are in time_zone, the user's mailbox zone. On time_zone_source "mailbox_utc" or
"fallback", confirm the zone before stating times.

A slot can include busy or out-of-office attendees; say a time works for everyone only when
availability_count shows all free. Working elsewhere counts as free.

No suggestions is not an error; empty_reason and note explain it.

parameters.name: attendee_emails
parameters.description: Email addresses of the people to meet, excluding yourself. Up to 20.

parameters.name: start_date_time
parameters.description: The start of the search window in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Timezone offset is ignored; the user's calendar timezone is used.

parameters.name: end_date_time
parameters.description: The end of the search window in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Timezone offset is ignored; the user's calendar timezone is used. The window must be less than 62 days.

parameters.name: meeting_duration_minutes
parameters.description: Length of the meeting in minutes. Defaults to 30.

parameters.name: max_candidates
parameters.description: Maximum number of suggestions to return, 1-20. Defaults to 5.

parameters.name: require_my_attendance
parameters.description: Whether you must be free for a slot to be suggested. Defaults to true.

parameters.name: hours
parameters.description: working: your working hours (default Mon-Fri 8am-5pm); personal: working hours plus weekends; all_hours: any time. Defaults to working.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: ForwardEvent
tools.description:
Send a meeting invitation to someone who is not invited yet; they join the attendee list and the organizer is told.

Works on a meeting you organize or one you were invited to. The attendee list can be edited
only on a meeting you organize, so for someone else's meeting this is the way to bring another
person in. Any bounce goes to the organizer. Refused for a cancelled meeting, the whole series
of a repeating meeting (forward one date by its own event_id), and an event nobody else is
invited to.

Name the meeting by event_id or by event_subject. Only events in your own mailbox, and a
subject is looked up in your default calendar only.

parameters.name: recipient_emails
parameters.description: Email addresses to send the invitation to, as plain addresses such as name@example.com. Each one not already invited joins the meeting's attendee list. At least one.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: Identifier of the meeting to forward, exactly as an earlier read returned it. Give this or event_subject, not both. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: event_subject
parameters.description: Text from the subject of the meeting to forward, matched case-insensitively against events in the search window. Only your default calendar is searched, so an event kept on another one is reachable by event_id but not by subject. Nothing is sent unless exactly one event matches. Give this or event_id, not both. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: search_start_date_time
parameters.description: Start of the window an event_subject lookup scans, in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Any timezone offset is ignored and the wall clock is read in the mailbox's timezone. Ignored when event_id is given. Defaults to None (7 days ago).

parameters.name: search_end_date_time
parameters.description: End of the window an event_subject lookup scans, in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Any timezone offset is ignored and the wall clock is read in the mailbox's timezone. The window may not exceed 90 days. Ignored when event_id is given. Defaults to None (30 days from now).

parameters.name: note
parameters.description: Text included verbatim in the forwarded invitation. Blank means no note. Defaults to None.

output.description: The meeting as read before forwarding, who it was sent to, who was already invited, and how the meeting was found.

note.value: Hi, please join us for this important meeting. Looking forward to your input!

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: GetEvent
tools.description:
Get one event from the user's calendar, with everything known about it.

Returns an EventDetail: the event's subject, full body, times, location,
organizer and attendees, plus change_key (the token identifying which version
of the event this is), event_type and series_master_id (which together say
whether this is a one-off event, one date of a recurring series, or the series
itself), and online_meeting_join_url (the link that joins the online meeting,
distinct from web_link, which opens the event in Outlook).

Both forms of the description come back: body is the plain text with markup
stripped, and body_html is the stored markup, whole, which a listing row does not
carry at all. Take body_html when the formatting, links or lists matter, and
supply it as the body of a new event with body_format set to html, or it is
stored as literal text. An event with no description still returns a non-empty
body_html, because Outlook stores an empty scaffold; body being empty is what says
there is no agenda.

Use this to read an event in full, or after a listing to see a body the
listing only summarised.

start, end, organizer and response_status always come back, with their own
fields empty when Microsoft Graph returned no underlying object. An empty
start is a value the event is missing, not an event that is missing.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: The ID of the event to get

output.description: The event with its full body.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: GetSchedule
tools.description:
Get free/busy and calendar items in a time window for one or more people. Use it to check
a specific time. It does not propose or rank slots across a range, nor count who is free per
slot.

Times are in time_zone, the user's mailbox zone, which may be a Windows name such as "Eastern
Standard Time". On time_zone_source "mailbox_utc" or "fallback", treat times as unconfirmed
and check the intended zone before acting.

availability_view has one digit per interval from start_date_time: 0 = free or working
elsewhere, 1 = tentative, 2 = busy, 3 = out of office. schedule_items can extend past the
window. working_hours are on each person's own clock.

visibility is "readable" (an item overlaps the window), "free_on_primary_calendar" (no events
on the primary calendar; secondary calendars are not visible, so not proof of free), "denied"
(no permission), or "error" (see the row's error). Subject, location and is_private appear
only when shared with you.

parameters.name: email_addresses
parameters.description: Email addresses whose free/busy availability to check - people, rooms, resources, or distribution lists. Up to 20 entities per call, where a distribution list counts as every one of its members, so prefer naming individuals when the membership is known. Split larger groups across multiple calls. Repeated addresses are ignored, so the result may cover fewer people than were passed.

parameters.name: start_date_time
parameters.description: The start of the window to check, in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Timezone offset is ignored; the authenticated user's calendar timezone is used.

parameters.name: end_date_time
parameters.description: The end of the window to check, in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Timezone offset is ignored; the authenticated user's calendar timezone is used. The window must be less than 62 days.

parameters.name: availability_view_interval
parameters.description: Duration in minutes of each slot in the availability_view string (5-1440). Defaults to 30.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: ListCalendars
tools.description:
List all calendars the user has access to.

Returns the user's own calendars plus any shared or delegated calendars.
Each calendar includes its ID, name, owner, and permissions.

Use a calendar_id from the results to target a specific calendar
in other calendar tools.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of calendars to return. Max is 200. Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: pagination_token
parameters.description: The pagination token to continue a previous request.

output.description: One page of calendars. pagination_token is absent, not empty, when no further page exists.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: ListEventAttachments
tools.description:
List attachment metadata for a calendar event.

Returns metadata only (name, size, type, etc.). Attachment content is not included.
Use this tool when the user wants to know what files are attached to a calendar event
or meeting.

Pass a calendar_id to list attachments on events in shared or delegated calendars.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: The ID of the calendar event to list attachments for.

parameters.name: calendar_id
parameters.description: ID of a specific calendar containing the event, including shared and delegated ones. When omitted, searches the user's default calendar.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of attachments to return. Max is 100. Defaults to 25.

parameters.name: pagination_token
parameters.description: The pagination token to continue a previous request.

output.description: Attachment metadata without the file bytes. calendar_id is echoed back only when the lookup named a calendar.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: ListEventsInTimeRange
tools.description:
List everything on the user's calendar between two times.

Use this when the request is about a stretch of the calendar -- what is on
today, this week, between two clock times -- rather than about a property of
one particular event, which a filtered search answers better.

Returns a ListEventsResult: an events list of EventListItem rows, a num_events
count and truncated_by. Each row carries a short plain-text summary of the event
as its body, not the full description -- read the event by its event_id to get the
body in full. body_has_formatting says whether the description holds links, lists
or styling that the stripped text cannot carry; a row never carries the markup
itself, so read the event by its event_id when that formatting matters. Each row
also carries the event_type and series_master_id that say whether it is a one-off
event, one date of a recurring series, or the series itself.

truncated_by is limit when Microsoft Graph offered another page, which usually
but not always means more events remain, and empty when it offered none and the
list is the whole window. No continuation cursor is issued, so narrow the window
to reach the rest, or raise limit while it is below its maximum. An empty list
with an empty truncated_by means nothing is scheduled in this window.

Ignores timezone offsets provided in the start_date_time and end_date_time parameters.
Instead, uses the user's default calendar timezone to filter events.
If the user has not set a timezone for their calendar, then the timezone will be UTC.

parameters.name: start_date_time
parameters.description: The start date and time of the time range, represented in ISO 8601 format. Timezone offset is ignored. For example, 2025-04-24T19:00:00

parameters.name: end_date_time
parameters.description: The end date and time of the time range, represented in ISO 8601 format. Timezone offset is ignored. For example, 2025-04-24T19:30:00

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of events to return. Max 1000. Defaults to 10

output.description: Events overlapping the requested window, each body a short summary rather than the full description. truncated_by says whether the window holds more than came back.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: RemoveEventFromMyCalendar
tools.description:
Take an event off your calendar without emailing anyone.

For a meeting someone else organizes, or your own appointment with no
invitees. Other attendees keep their copies. An organizer in your organization
sees you declined; one outside it is not told. Refused for a meeting you
organize with invitees. Irreversible.

Use is_organizer, attendees, event_type and series_master_id from an earlier
read to choose this tool and scope. A cancelled meeting stays on your calendar
with is_cancelled true, and listings hide it unless asked. Only events in your
own mailbox, not shared or delegated calendars.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: The event's event_id, exactly as an earlier read returned it.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: For a repeating event: instance (this date) or series (every date). Required when it repeats; omit otherwise.

output.description: The event as read before removal, the caller's role, what the organizer sees, and the scope applied.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: RespondToEvent
tools.description:
Accept, decline or tentatively accept a meeting someone else invited you to, and tell the organizer.

Declining takes the meeting off your calendar unless Show declined events is turned on in
Outlook, and once it is gone it cannot be answered again from here. Refused for a meeting
you organize, a cancelled meeting, and the whole series of a repeating meeting: answer one
date by its own event_id.

Name the meeting by event_id or by event_subject. Only events in your own mailbox, and a
subject is looked up in your default calendar only.

parameters.name: response
parameters.description: Your answer: accepted, declined or tentative.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: Identifier of the meeting to answer, exactly as an earlier read returned it. Give this or event_subject, not both. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: event_subject
parameters.description: Text from the subject of the meeting to answer, matched case-insensitively against events in the search window. Only your default calendar is searched, so an event kept on another one is reachable by event_id but not by subject. Nothing is sent unless exactly one event matches. Give this or event_id, not both. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: search_start_date_time
parameters.description: Start of the window an event_subject lookup scans, in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Any timezone offset is ignored and the wall clock is read in the mailbox's timezone. Ignored when event_id is given. Defaults to None (7 days ago).

parameters.name: search_end_date_time
parameters.description: End of the window an event_subject lookup scans, in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Any timezone offset is ignored and the wall clock is read in the mailbox's timezone. The window may not exceed 90 days. Ignored when event_id is given. Defaults to None (30 days from now).

parameters.name: note
parameters.description: Text sent to the organizer with your reply, verbatim. Blank means no note. Needs notify_organizer true. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: notify_organizer
parameters.description: Whether the organizer is emailed your reply. A note or a proposed time is only delivered when this is true. Set false to record your answer on your own calendar only; the organizer's tracking then keeps showing no reply. Required when the organizer did not ask for replies. Defaults to True.

parameters.name: proposed_start_date_time
parameters.description: A different start to suggest to the organizer, as a full ISO 8601 date and time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Take the date from the meeting as read; do not assume today. Any timezone offset is ignored and the wall clock is read in the mailbox's timezone. Only with declined or tentative, only when the organizer allows new times, and only with notify_organizer true. Defaults to None (no new time proposed).

parameters.name: proposed_end_date_time
parameters.description: End of the suggested time, in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS), read the same way. Needs proposed_start_date_time. Defaults to None (keeps the meeting's current length).

output.description: The meeting after your answer, whether the answer was confirmed, and how the meeting was found.

note.value: I should be able to make it, but please note I may be 10 minutes late.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: SearchEvents
tools.description:
Find calendar events by what is true about them: subject text, who attends,
who organised them, importance, or whether they are online.

Use this when the request names a property of the event. When the request is
about a stretch of the calendar instead -- what is on Tuesday, this week's
meetings -- reading the whole time range fits better, because this search
covers only a 90-day window either side of today unless dates are given.

Returns a SearchEventsResult: an events list of SearchEventItem rows plus
num_events, searched_window, truncated_by, and the filter_expression /
client_side_filters that say where each filter was applied.

Results are in chronological order. Each row carries a short plain-text
summary of the event as its body, not the full description. Read one event
by its event_id to get the body in full.

An empty events list means nothing matched inside searched_window; it does not
mean no such event exists. Widen the range or drop a filter before reporting
that there is none. On truncated_by scan_cap the scan stopped early and no
continuation token is issued, so narrow the window or the filters instead of
paging -- an empty list there says even less.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: Filter events whose subject contains this text (case-insensitive). Defaults to None (no subject filter).

parameters.name: attendee_emails
parameters.description: Filter events that include these attendees by exact email address. Multiple emails are combined with AND (all must be attendees). Defaults to None (no attendee filter).

parameters.name: organizer_name
parameters.description: Filter events organized by another specific person by their display name. Matching is case-insensitive substring against the organizer's display name. Do not use this to filter for events organized by the current authenticated user — use organized_by_me=True instead, which does not depend on knowing your own display name. Defaults to None (no organizer filter).

parameters.name: organized_by_me
parameters.description: Filter for events the current authenticated user organized (True) vs. events the current user was invited to but did not organize (False). Defaults to None (no filter). Prefer this over organizer_name when the user asks about their own events — it does not require knowing the user's display name in the tenant's format.

parameters.name: importance
parameters.description: Filter by event importance level. Defaults to None (no filter).

parameters.name: is_online_meeting
parameters.description: Filter on Outlook's own online-meeting flag: True keeps events Outlook hosts a meeting for, False keeps the rest. False is not the same as in person -- an event run on a link pasted into its body is flagged False. Defaults to None (no filter).

parameters.name: start_date_time
parameters.description: The start of the time range, in ISO 8601 format. Timezone offset is ignored; the user's calendar timezone is used. Defaults to None (90 days before today).

parameters.name: end_date_time
parameters.description: The end of the time range, in ISO 8601 format. Timezone offset is ignored; the user's calendar timezone is used. Defaults to None (90 days after today).

parameters.name: calendar_id
parameters.description: ID of a specific calendar to search, including shared and delegated ones. When omitted, searches the user's default calendar.

parameters.name: include_cancelled
parameters.description: Whether to include cancelled events in the results. Defaults to False.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of matching events to return. Max is 200. Defaults to 25. When client-side filters are active, the tool may scan multiple pages to accumulate matches.

parameters.name: pagination_token
parameters.description: Encoded pagination token to continue a previous request. Preserves client-side filter state (attendee_emails, organizer_name, organized_by_me, is_online_meeting) across continuation calls.

output.description: One page of matches, each body a short summary rather than the full description. searched_window is the range this search asked Graph for. truncated_by says why the list ended, and on scan_cap no continuation token is issued -- narrow the window rather than paging. filter_expression and client_side_filters say where each filter ran.

codeExample.tabLabel: Call the Tool with User Authorization

tools.name: UpdateEvent
tools.description:
Change one event in the user's calendar, in place.

Returns an UpdateEventResult: the updated event in full, plus changed and
fields_changed (what was actually written, which is nothing when the event
already said what was asked for), change_key, concurrency_checked,
applied_scope, online_meeting_preserved, attendees_not_found, and the record
of how the event was resolved.

Everyone invited is mailed an updated invitation for any change this writes,
so an edit to a meeting with guests is not a quiet one.

Every input left out leaves that part of the event alone, so this changes
only what is named and never cancels, deletes or re-creates the event.
Adding or dropping a guest is merged over the people already invited rather
than replacing them; set_attendee_emails states the whole invitation list and
replaces it. An event that turns out to be a recurring series itself is
refused: edit one of its dates instead.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: Identifier of the event to change, exactly as an earlier read returned it. Give this or event_subject, not both. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: event_subject
parameters.description: Text from the subject of the event to change, matched case-insensitively against events in the search window. Only your default calendar is searched, so an event kept on another one is reachable by event_id but not by subject. Use this when the event is known by what it is called rather than by an identifier. Nothing is changed unless exactly one event matches. Give this or event_id, not both. Defaults to None.

parameters.name: search_start_date_time
parameters.description: Start of the window an event_subject lookup scans, in ISO 8601 format. Any timezone offset is ignored and the wall clock is read in the mailbox's timezone. Ignored when event_id is given. Defaults to None (7 days ago).

parameters.name: search_end_date_time
parameters.description: End of the window an event_subject lookup scans, in ISO 8601 format. Any timezone offset is ignored and the wall clock is read in the mailbox's timezone. The window may not exceed 90 days. Ignored when event_id is given. Defaults to None (30 days from now).

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: New title for the event. This is what the event is called, not what it says -- the description is body. Pass an empty string to leave the event untitled. Defaults to None (the title is left unchanged).

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: New description for the event, replacing the existing one rather than adding to it. To keep the formatting of a description that was read, pass that event's body_html here and set body_format to html: its body field is the same description with every link, list and emphasis stripped out, so passing that instead silently flattens it. Otherwise pass the text to store, with line breaks kept. On a meeting, the block that makes it joinable is carried over and the response says what survived, so an empty string clears the words but leaves that block rather than emptying the description. Defaults to None (the description is left unchanged).

parameters.name: start_date_time
parameters.description: New start for the event, in ISO 8601 format, for example 2026-04-25T13:00:00. Any timezone offset is ignored: the wall clock given is the wall clock the event lands on, read in time_zone or the mailbox's own timezone. Naming only this keeps the existing end. Defaults to None (the start is left unchanged).

parameters.name: end_date_time
parameters.description: New end for the event, in ISO 8601 format. Any timezone offset is ignored. Naming only this keeps the existing start, which is how a meeting is shortened or extended. Defaults to None (the end is left unchanged).

parameters.name: time_zone
parameters.description: Timezone the new start and end wall clocks should be read in, as a Windows zone name such as Eastern Standard Time or an IANA name such as America/New_York. Needs start_date_time or end_date_time beside it, since a zone on its own reaches neither end of the event; whichever of the two is left out keeps the moment it already runs at. Defaults to None (the mailbox's own timezone).

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: New location for the event, replacing whatever is there. This is where people go, not where an online meeting lives. A room booked through Outlook cannot be written over from here -- Outlook replaces the whole place when a new one is written, which would turn the booking into plain text -- so such a change is refused. Pass an empty string to clear it. Defaults to None (the location is left unchanged).

parameters.name: is_all_day
parameters.description: Whether the event should occupy whole days rather than a clock time. Changing this needs start_date_time and end_date_time given alongside it, and when true both must fall at midnight, the end being the day after the last day the event covers. Defaults to None (left unchanged).

parameters.name: show_as
parameters.description: How the event should show to people checking the organizer's availability. Outlook labels this Show As. Defaults to None (left unchanged).

parameters.name: importance
parameters.description: New priority for the event. Defaults to None (left unchanged).

parameters.name: reminder_minutes_before_start
parameters.description: How many minutes before the start the reminder should fire. Outlook keeps the alert and its lead time as two separate settings, so asking for a reminder here turns the alert on as well -- an event carrying this lead time with its alert off is still changed. Defaults to None (left unchanged).

parameters.name: attendee_emails_to_add
parameters.description: Email addresses to invite, added to the people already invited. Everyone else keeps their place and the reply they gave. Defaults to None (nobody is added).

parameters.name: attendees_to_remove
parameters.description: People to uninvite, each given as an email address or as whole words from a person's name -- a first name, a surname, or both, matched against the names the guests are listed under. Part of a word does not match, so Sam does not reach Samantha. A name matching more than one guest is refused rather than guessed, an entry matching nobody is reported back while the rest of the edit still applies, and everyone actually uninvited is named in the response. Defaults to None (nobody is removed).

parameters.name: set_attendee_emails
parameters.description: The complete list of email addresses that should be invited, replacing everyone currently on the event. Anyone already invited keeps the kind of invitation they hold, so an optional guest stays optional. Leaving a booked room off the list is refused, since that would release its booking. Pass an empty list to uninvite everyone. Cannot be combined with attendee_emails_to_add or attendees_to_remove. Defaults to None (the invitation list is left unchanged).

parameters.name: expected_change_key
parameters.description: The change_key of the event version being edited, from a read taken immediately beforehand. When given, the edit is refused if the event moved on since that read, and nothing is written. Defaults to None, which writes without a version check -- whatever is there is overwritten.

parameters.name: body_format
parameters.description: The form the body argument is written in. Set html only when the body you are passing actually carries HTML tags, as the body_html of an event that was read does -- declaring html over plain words stores them marked as markup and they render wrong. plain_text stores the body as written, escaping anything that looks like markup. Ignored when body is left out. Defaults to plain_text.

output.description: The event as it stands after the edit, with what was written, whether the write ran under a version check, and how the event was found.

body.value: Please review the updated agenda before joining. Dial-in details remain the same.

tools.description:
Get information about the current user and their Outlook Calendar environment.

mailbox_timezone is the time zone this mailbox's dates are expressed in. It may be a
Windows name such as "Eastern Standard Time" rather than an IANA identifier - that
names a zone observing daylight saving, not a fixed offset. mailbox_timezone_source
says where it came from: "mailbox" and "mailbox_utc" mean the mailbox itself names
the zone, whereas "default_not_configured" (the mailbox names none) and
"default_unreadable" (the setting could not be read) mean UTC is a fallback this
toolkit applied, not a zone the mailbox is set to. On either fallback, do not tell
the user their mailbox is configured for that zone.

summary:
## Microsoft Outlook Calendar Toolkit

The Microsoft Outlook Calendar toolkit provides Arcade LLM tools for reading and managing a user's Outlook Calendar via Microsoft Graph, enabling agents to query, create, update, and respond to calendar events on behalf of authenticated users.

## Capabilities

- **Event discovery & inspection:** List events across a time range, search events by property (subject, attendees, organizer, importance, online status), get a single event in full detail including rich HTML body, and retrieve attachment metadata.
- **Scheduling & availability:** Find meeting times across a group of attendees (ranked suggestions, no booking), and check free/busy status for specific time windows across one or more people.
- **Event creation & modification:** Create new events with plain-text or HTML bodies, update individual events in place (field-level merges, attendee list management), and target shared or delegated calendars where supported.
- **Meeting actions:** Accept, tentatively accept, or decline meeting invitations with organizer notification; forward meetings to new attendees; cancel organized meetings with cancellation emails to all invitees.
- **Calendar & identity context:** List all accessible calendars (own, shared, delegated) with IDs and permissions; retrieve current user profile and mailbox timezone metadata to correctly interpret event times.
- **Scope and safety guardrails:** Tools enforce organizer/attendee role checks, recurring-series scoping, irreversibility warnings (cancel, remove), and timezone handling based on mailbox configuration.

## OAuth

This toolkit uses OAuth 2.0 via the **Microsoft** provider. See the [Arcade Microsoft auth provider docs](https://docs.arcade.dev/en/references/auth-providers/microsoft) for setup details.
